reviewers: 3 fresh Opus 5.5, parallel; a major counts only if 2 of 3 raise it
note: hd-stairs-down majority was caused by a wrong brief (it was described as DOWN); the clock/stairwell majors were real and led to the redraw judged in r13.

majors: Bottom two treads are big brown rectangles with gold outline trim and dot specks inside a framed alcove, under a glowing gold bar: at 1x and 3x the whole thing reads as a dresser/chest of drawers in a wardrobe niche (same wood as the shipped wardrobe), not a climbing stair
minors: Gold-studded blue frame is busier than the shipped wizarding kits
The two bottom treads are boxed by gold/blue outline rectangles that read like drawer fronts; the whole framed alcove is close to a chest of drawers
The bright gold band at the top reads like lamp/hearth glow more than a landing

majors: at 1x, and still at 3x, the stack of equal brown slabs with dark gaps inside a studded box frame with a top lintel reads as a chest of drawers or bookshelf, not a stair; there is no runner, side rail or clear narrowing to signal a climb
minors: the gold studs along the frame read as furniture trim, which adds to the cabinet impression
Bottom treads protrude beyond the door jambs; acceptable but frame posts then appear to float above the outer treads
Glowing gold strip at the top is shared with all UP pieces and reads a bit like a lamp/oven glow
The red runner carries the read; without it the grey treads in an arched dark frame would look like a shelf
the frame header and posts give it a furniture-box silhouette; only the red runner tells the player it is a stair
Wooden L-brackets at the bottom treads make the lower steps read like stacked crates
Stray single light pixel on the bottom tread
Grey treads are low-contrast against the grey interior; at 1x the steps merge into one slab
Single white speck on a bottom tread reads as a stray pixel
at 1x the grey bands inside the wood frame lean toward a shelf; the rough stone speckle is barely visible
the white speck at the lower right reads as a stray pixel or object

majors: Drawn with the exact UP composition (glowing gold landing at the top/back, treads widening toward the viewer, inside the same arched alcove as wz-clock-stair); nothing indicates descent into a hole, so a player reads it as an up staircase (or the same drawer-cabinet as clock-stair)

Labelled DOWN but drawn exactly like the UP pieces: arched frame, glowing gold landing at the top (north), treads stacking up toward it with the bottom steps protruding forward. A player reads it as stairs going UP; nothing shows a hole or descent (compare castle/owl-stair-down)
laid out identically to the UP pieces (bright gold landing band at the top, treads growing toward the viewer), so the player reads it as an up stair; nothing shows descent into a hole
minors: the dark brown right side wall is heavier than the left, so the piece looks unbalanced

majors: The hole rim is drawn as an upright frame with posts reaching the ground and horizontal dark slats in the upper interior; at 1x/3x it reads as a fireplace/stove or floor grate, not a stairwell opening in the floor
minors: Only the bottom 2 steps are legible; the rest is near-black bars

majors: A square stone frame around a dark interior, with horizontal grey bars and a light slab at the bottom: at 1x and 3x it reads as a fireplace/oven mouth or a floor grate, not a stairwell. No tread/riser alternation is legible in the dark top half, and the light bottom slab reads as a hearth stone
minors: It is shorter than the UP pieces and sits on the floor like a free-standing box rather than a cut into the floor

majors: a stone-framed dark opening with a few grey steps at the bottom reads as a fireplace or hearth (or an oven grate), not a stairwell going down north; at 1x it is a dark framed box
minors: the steps are low-contrast grey on dark, so the tread top and riser split is barely visible

majors: Wooden upright frame around a dark box with gray slabs at the bottom reads as a hearth/oven or open crate at 1x and 3x rather than a hole in the floor descending north
minors: Stray white pixel on the bottom step

majors: Same hearth/grate read as castle-stair-down: a wooden frame, a dark mouth with horizontal slats, and a white fleck on the bottom slab that reads as ash or ember. It looks like a fireplace or stove, not a descending stair
a wood-framed dark box with grey steps at the bottom and a white speck reads as a fireplace with an ember or bone, not a descending stair
minors: the white speck in the lower middle looks like a stray object
